title: Employment & Litigation Legal Assistant
description:
Legal Assistant - Employment & Litigation

Location: York (with occasional travel between offices)
Salary: Competitive + Benefits
Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

The Opportunity

An established and highly respected regional law firm is seeking a proactive and organised Legal Assistant to join its Employment & Litigation team.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to develop their legal career within a supportive, professional environment. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting fee earners, managing client onboarding, progressing legal matters, and ensuring excellent client service throughout the lifecycle of a case.

The role combines legal administration, compliance responsibilities and hands-on case support, making it ideal for an ambitious individual with previous legal experience or a strong interest in litigation and employment law.

Key Responsibilities
Client Onboarding & Matter Management
- Open and maintain client files using the firm's case management system.
- Create and manage matter records and ensure documentation is accurately recorded.
- Coordinate the issuance and return of client care documentation and engagement paperwork.
- Manage electronic signature processes and client onboarding administration.
- Act as a key point of contact for clients throughout the lifespan of a matter.

Compliance & Risk
- Conduct identity verification and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) checks.
- Maintain accurate compliance records and client documentation.
- Liaise with internal compliance teams regarding queries or potential concerns.
- Ensure client information is handled confidentially and in accordance with regulatory requirements.
- Support continuous improvement of processes and systems.

Litigation & Employment Support
- Assist fee earners in progressing a varied caseload.
- Draft legal correspondence and documentation under supervision.
- Organise and review client documents and case papers.
- Prepare bills, invoices and associated financial records.
- Undertake basic legal research and support case preparation activities.
- Ensure all work is completed in accordance with firm procedures and quality standards.

File Closure & Administration
- Coordinate file closure procedures and record maintenance.
- Ensure all compliance and financial matters are concluded appropriately.
- Support archiving and retrieval of both physical and electronic files.
- Assist with diary management, correspondence, filing and general administrative duties.
- Provide occasional reception cover when required.

About You

The successful candidate will possess:
- Previous experience within a law firm, legal support, compliance or professional services environment.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- High levels of attention to detail and accuracy.
- Experience using Microsoft Office, particularly Word and Excel.
- Confidence working with digital document management and case management systems.
- A client-focused approach with a professional and empathetic manner.
- The ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
- A proactive attitude and willingness to learn and develop professionally.

Desirable Experience
- Experience supporting Employment, Litigation or Dispute Resolution teams.
- Knowledge of AML and client onboarding procedures.
- Familiarity with legal document drafting and case administration.
- Experience of electronic case management systems.

What's On Offer?
- The opportunity to join a well-established and reputable regional law firm.
- Exposure to a broad range of Employment and Litigation matters.
- Supportive team environment and ongoing professional development.
- Genuine opportunities for progression and career growth.
- Competitive salary and benefits package.

To apply, please submit your CV for confidential consideration.

Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age.

title: Education Delivery Coordinator, Alternative Provision North Yorkshire (new Yorkshire office opening early 2027)
description:
Education Delivery Coordinator, Alternative Provision North Yorkshire (new Yorkshire office opening early 2027) £30,000 - £35,000 basic OTE £50,000 - £65,000 year one

Some children cannot thrive in mainstream school. At AP Education, named National Tutoring Company of the Year, more than 500 of them learn with us every day, and we are bringing that work to more young people across North Yorkshire with a new Yorkshire office opening in early 2027. If you come from teaching, tutoring, SEND or pastoral work, this role lets you keep shaping outcomes outside the classroom.

The role

You will coordinate bespoke tuition programmes for learners who cannot access mainstream education or need a more individual approach. You will be the link between Local Authorities, tutors and families, making sure every young person receives consistent, high-quality support.

What you will do
- Understand each learner's needs and make sure the provision we arrange meets them.
- Match tutors and education support professionals to learners, based on skills, experience and availability.
- Stay in regular contact with tutors and families, and visit settings and homes to review attendance, engagement and progress.
- Work with Local Authorities, schools, Virtual Schools and SEND teams.
- Spot challenges early and work with everyone involved to solve them.

Where you will work
- Three weeks of funded training at our head office in Harlow, Essex, to start. (accommodation will be provided)
- Home-based across York, Harrogate, Scarborough, Northallerton and the rest of North Yorkshire until the office opens, then based at our new Yorkshire office which opens in early 2027.
- Regular travel to schools, settings and learners' homes, with mileage included. You will report to the Education Manager.

What we are looking for

Essential:
- Experience in education, ideally Alternative Provision, SEND or SEMH.
- An understanding of the challenges facing children and young people who struggle to access mainstream education.
- Excellent communication skills, with the confidence to work with families, tutors and professionals.
- Self-discipline and the ability to work independently.
- A calm, solutions-focused approach to challenging situations.
- A full driving licence and access to a vehicle.

Desirable:
- Experience in recruitment, relationship management or a similar role.

Why AP Education

AP Education is the National Tutoring Company of the Year. More than 500 children who cannot access mainstream school learn with us every day. We are growing fast, and our new Yorkshire office opens in early 2027. Our culture is family first: demanding, but supportive and kind.
- £30,000 - £35,000 basic plus commission, with on-target earnings (OTE) of £50,000 - £65,000 in year one.
- Three weeks of funded training, then ongoing development.
- A structured career progression framework, with real room to move up as the new office grows.
- Benefits package including - private healthcare after 36 months service, gym membership, pension, mileage scheme, full equipment provided - laptop and phone etc.

How to apply

Please apply via this advert, or get in touch directly with our Head of People Jennie McElhatton at (url removed)

This role is subject to an enhanced DBS check. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, and we welcome applications from all backgrounds.

title: Care & Support Coordinator
description:
Care & Support Coordinator

Location: Harrogate

Salary: £16.10 per hour

Are you organised, proactive and passionate about delivering high-quality, person-centred care? We would love to hear from you!

We are recruiting for a Care & Support Coordinator to provide cover across weekdays, evenings and weekends. We welcome applications from candidates seeking either full-time or part-time employment.

Whether you are looking for full-time hours, part-time work, we would be pleased to hear from you.

About the Role

We are looking for a dedicated and experienced Care & Support Coordinator to join our team and play a key role in the effective planning and delivery of our care and support services.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with experience in social care who enjoys coordinating people, supporting staff and ensuring customers receive high-quality, consistent and personalised care.

Working closely with the Manager, Deputy Manager, staff, customers, families and other professionals, you will support the smooth day-to-day running of the service, ensuring that care and support are effectively coordinated and individual needs are met.

You will play an important role in ensuring the right staff are in the right place at the right time, while promoting a person-centred approach that places customers' rights, choices, wishes and independence at the heart of everything we do.

Key Responsibilities

Care Planning and Coordination
- Plan, book and coordinate care and support visits.
- Coordinate and manage staff rotas, ensuring appropriate staffing levels and cover across the service.
- Allocate staff to customers, taking account of individual needs, staff skills, experience, location and compatibility.
- Ensure all rota changes are updated promptly and accurately on the rostering system.
- Assess and process referrals and coordinate the onboarding of new customers.
- Develop, review and maintain customer support plans and risk assessments.
- Maintain effective communication with customers, families, staff and other professionals involved in the delivery of care and support.

Service Quality and Staff Support
- Support the Manager with the effective day-to-day running of the care and support service.
- Promote and monitor the delivery of high-quality, personalised care and support.
- Undertake spot checks and staff supervisions as required.
- Support recruitment and selection activities.
- Manage staff absence procedures, including conducting return-to-work interviews.
- Promote a positive, supportive and professional working environment.

Operational Responsibilities
- Respond to emergency call bells and provide background support when working at St Roberts Grove.
- Provide cover for care and support calls when required.
- Participate in an out-of-hours on-call rota.
- Attend staff meetings, supervision sessions and training as required.
- Promote a positive image of the organisation, its work and values.
- Maintain compliance with organisational policies and procedures, including relevant health and safety requirements.

What We Are Looking For

We are seeking someone who is proactive, reliable and well organised, with the ability to manage competing priorities, use their initiative and work effectively as part of a team.

You will have good communication and administrative skills, an understanding of the social care sector and the confidence to coordinate staff and respond effectively to the changing needs of the service.

Essential Requirements

Skills and Competencies
- Good verbal and written communication skills.
- Ability to plan, organise and coordinate staff rotas effectively.
- Strong administrative skills and good computer literacy.
- Ability to maintain accurate records and follow statutory reporting procedures.
- Ability to understand, implement and follow policies, procedures and instructions.

Experience
- Experience of working within the social care sector.
- Previous experience of coordinating staff rotas.

Qualifications and Knowledge
- Minimum Level 2 qualification in Health and Social Care, with a willingness to work towards Level 3.
- Knowledge of health and safety within care services, including risk assessment and management.
- Understanding of safeguarding, including the ability to recognise signs of abuse and follow the appropriate reporting procedures.

Additional Requirements
- Willingness to work flexibly to meet the changing needs of the service.
- Commitment to keeping knowledge, skills and professional practice up to date.
- Willingness to undertake an Enhanced DBS check.

Desirable Requirements
- Experience of staff management or supervision.
- Experience of using care management or rostering systems.
- Full, valid UK driving licence.

What We Offer

This is an opportunity to make a real difference to the lives of the people we support while developing your skills and experience within a rewarding social care environment.

You will be joining a team that is committed to promoting independence, dignity, choice and high-quality, person-centred care.

Equality, Diversity and Inclusion

We are committed to promoting equality, diversity and inclusion and welcome applications from all sections of the community.

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Disability Action Yorkshire, please do not hesitate to apply.

title: Provisioning Coordinator
description:
Job Title: Provisioning Coordinator
Location: Harrogate
Salary: £30,000 - £35,000 per annum
Hours: Monday - Friday 9:00am - 5:30pm

We are seeking a proactive Provisioning Coordinator to support the end to end delivery of telecommunications circuits and services. This role is key to ensuring accurate, timely provisioning across multiple customer projects while maintaining strong supplier and stakeholder relationships.

- Support reporting and data accuracy requirements
- Identify and escalate risks or delays early

- Support continuous improvement initiatives

Experience Required:
- Experience in provisioning, telecoms, service delivery or coordination role
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
- Excellent organisation and ability to manage multiple tasks
- High attention to detail and accuracy
- Proactive, customer focused and self motivated
- Competent in Microsoft Office and internal systems

In return, the successful Provisioning Coordinator will benefit from a competitive salary of £30,000 - £35,000 per annum, Hybrid Working, excellent company benefits, ongoing training and development opportunities, a supportive working environment and the opportunity to build a long term career within a growing business. title: Admin Purchasing Assistant
description:
As an Admin Purchasing Assistant in Northallerton, you will manage day-to-day purchasing administration to help keep supplies and business records organised within the FMCG sector. You will work closely with the Secretarial & Business Support department, ensuring purchasing information is accurate and available when needed.

Client Details

The organisation operates in the FMCG sector in Northallerton.

Description
- Maintain accurate purchasing records, ensuring information is clearly filed and easy to retrieve.
- Process purchase-related administration in a timely manner to support smooth daily operations.
- Prepare and update purchasing documentation, keeping records complete and consistent.
- Check order details and administrative information to help reduce errors and delays.
- Communicate with internal colleagues to gather and share purchasing information.
- Monitor outstanding administrative tasks and follow them through to completion.
- Organise electronic and paper files to maintain clear purchasing documentation.
- Provide general administrative support within the Secretarial & Business Support department.

Profile

A successful 'Admin Purchasing Assistant' should have:
- Experience completing accurate administrative tasks in a busy office setting.
- Confidence maintaining records, documents and purchasing-related information.
- The ability to check details carefully and keep information up to date.
- Experience organising files and managing routine office administration.
- Clear written and verbal communication skills for working with colleagues.
- Confidence managing several tasks while keeping work organised.

Job Offer
- Fixed-term contract as an Admin Purchasing Assistant.
- Salary of 27,000 to 33,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Based in Northallerton.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

People are at the heart of Michael Page. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment. As an inclusive recruiter we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and experiences. If you require any adjustments or accommodations during the recruitment process, we'll work with you to ensure you can perform at your best.

title: Receptionist
description: Yorkshire Health Network are looking for a polite and helpful receptionist to work 37.5 hours a week as the first point of contact for the Clinical Services Team. The working hours are Monday - Friday, between the hours of 08:00 and 20:30 and a Saturday, 08:00 - 17:30. The post holder will responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and the provision of general support to the multidisciplinary team by ensuring all functions are carried out in accordance with agreed procedures, protocols and time-scales. Meet and greet patients and visitors arriving at the site and direct them accordingly. Responsible for visitors signing in and out of the building as required. Set up clinical and reception spaces and ensure that the waiting area is prepared prior to clinic commencing and is maintained to a high standard during the clinic. Book, cancel and amend appointments on the clinical system, send and actioning tasks, printing ICE forms, PDS updates, check patients in and out and send SMS reminders. Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers' request appropriately signposting patients to the correct service. Support clinical staff with the patient clinics including cancelling patients, rearranging appointments if necessary. Maintain confidentiality of patients. When required, to be responsible for the opening and closing of the building at the beginning and the end of the day, ensuring safety and security measures are followed. Chaperone duties as and when required Responsible for accepting clinical deliveries and ensure that they are put away in a timely manner and in fridges in order to maintain cold chain and safety. Check fridge temperature logs and daily oxygen and defib checks. Take payments for clinical service prior to appointment or at end of treatment. Arranging pathology samples to be collected by relevant organisations and ensuring they are correctly labelled.

title: Administrator - Receptionist
company: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
description: We are looking for an experienced, friendly and approachable receptionist to join our established front-of-house team at North Moor House in Northallerton. North Moor House is a new modern building providing outpatient facilities for people accessing mental health and learning disability services. As the first point of contact for service users, carers, staff and visitors, you will play an important role in creating a welcoming, supportive and professional environment. Free onsite parking is available. Previous customer service experience is essential, although NHS or healthcare experience is not required. We are looking for someone who genuinely enjoys helping people, works well with colleagues and brings a positive, proactive and flexible approach. This is an established afternoon position, working 25 hours per week, Monday to Friday. Shifts alternate between 12:30-17:30 and 13:00- 18:00. Occasional flexibility to cover morning reception during colleague's annual leave or sickness absence is required. You must have the Right to Work in the UK in order to be successfully appointed to this role. Please note, this role does not meet the required eligibility criteria for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker visa and therefore the Trust is unable to offer sponsorship for this particular role. Be the welcoming face of North moor House As part of our front-of-house team, you'll play an important role in creating a welcoming and supportive environment for everyone visiting North Moor House. Your day will involve greeting service users, carers and visitors, answering telephone enquiries and helping people find the information or assistance they need. Alongside these responsibilities, you'll undertake a variety of administrative and practical tasks that support the smooth running of the reception. These include maintaining visitor records and clinic lists, managing room bookings, receiving deliveries, handling post and petty cash, dealing with prescriptions and pathology collections, ordering stationery and reporting building maintenance issues. Working in mental health services can be both rewarding and challenging. Some people attending reception may be anxious, distressed or frustrated, and we are looking for someone who can remain calm, communicate sensitively and respond professionally in these situations You'll need to be organised, able to manage competing demands and confident communicating with a wide range of people, while maintaining confidentiality and a calm, professional approach. Interested in joining our team? Please read the job description and person specification carefully. In your application, tell us how you meet the essential criteria, providing examples of your skills and experience. What we can offer you Salary: £16,848 per annum (£25,272 full time equivalent) Joining our teams means becoming part of an organisation that recognises the important contribution our administrative professionals make to delivering high-quality patient care. We offer a generous NHS pension and annual leave entitlement of 27 days, increasing with NHS service, plus bank holidays (all calculated pro rata for part-time staff). You'll also have access to a range of staff benefits, including: NHS staff discounts across a wide range of retailers. Car lease scheme Access to Trust gyms Options to purchase up to 2 weeks additional leave Staff health & wellbeing support Monthly prize draw Staff recognition through our Greatix and Star Award schemes. A place where your contribution matters We recognise that our reception and administrative colleagues are an essential part of our services. Whether welcoming someone to their appointment, helping a colleague or ensuring the day runs smoothly, your contribution makes a difference. Through our Journey to Change , we're committed to creating a positive working environment where colleagues feel supported, valued and recognised for the work they do. Joining our team We want our colleagues to feel supported, valued and encouraged to develop. You'll have regular one-one supervision and an annual appraisal, providing opportunities to discuss your achievements, share ideas, explore challenges and consider your development. You'll be joining an established reception team, working alongside experienced colleagues and with the support of a dedicated Reception Supervisor. We'll provide a structured induction and clear guidance to help you settle into your role and build confidence in your responsibilities. Come and meet us! We understand that working in mental health services may be a new experience for some applicants. If you'd like to learn more about the role, ask questions or arrange an informal visit to North Moor House before applying, we'd be delighted to hear from you. Please contact Safina Beg, Reception Supervisor, on 01609 751269 We look forward to hearing from you! This job advert may close early if a high volume of applications have been received. If interested, please apply for this post as soon as possible.

title: Medical Administrator
description: A exciting opportunity has arisen at Scott Road Medical Centre, Selby for the role of Medical Administrator to work within our friendly administration team. We're looking for a multi skilled administrator with excellent keyboard skills and efficient in IT to work in a fast paced, busy office environment. Are you a committed individual who is a team player? Do you have a proactive attitude and are looking for a new challenge? If so then this could be the role for you... This position is a part time position, 21 hours over 3 days with working pattern as below; Monday 8.30am - 16.00pm Thursday 8.30am - 16.00pm Friday 8.30am - 16.00pm Personal specification Excellent communication skills, including a polite and friendly telephone manner, a solution-focused approach with a professional appearance a uniform allowance is provided. Good organisation skills with the ability to multi task, working accurately and methodically to meet deadlines An excellent command of the English language, both verbally and in writing Computer literate and able to use internet, email, Word, Excel A minimum of 1 years experience within a customer service environment A minimum of Maths and English GCSE or equivalent qualification. The ability to be flexible (within the overall hours) to cover for absent colleagues. Able to work in a team, but use their own initiative. Working Life You'll support the work of the department by taking on administrative and secretarial tasks for example: Typing Arrange meetings and take minutes Receive and initiate calls, dealing with appropriate enquiries Speak directly to patients and provide medical information, using practice guidance. Deal with post and emails You will have contact with patients and their families as well as health care staff and other administration staff *this list of responsibilities is not designed to be exclusive, but serves to illustrate the scope of the role. You will be required to take on additional duties appropriate to the role. Training & development You will get the training you need to do the job. This includes an introduction to the department, how to use the IT & phone equipment and the procedures to follow. You may be offered the chance to take a medical terminology course and IT courses for the systems we use. Knowledge of SystemOne clinical system would be desireable Job Summary: The post holder will be part of the Patient Support team delivering a wide range of administrative duties within the practice so as to provide the highest standard of service to colleagues and patients. Departmental responsibilities will include being part of the team whose members share the following: Are competent users of the practices electronic clinical system, SystmOne, so as to be able to book appointments appropriately, access patient records efficiently and to ensure accurate maintenance of patient records Ensure that all incoming paper based patient information is scanned into the electronic system Ensure that the referral management process into both primary and secondary care operates efficiently and referrals are dealt with according to strict time scales Action tasks set by clinicians via computer system and emails. Communicate with patients face to face and via the telephone in a manner that upholds the reputation of the practice Process prescription requests which come into the practice in a variety of ways. This involves using the prescribing system, both manual and electronic, accurately and efficiently, ensuring at all times that the protocol is followed Staff the clinical results telephone line, providing test results to patients as directed by the practice GPs Process appointment requests from patients in person or by telephone Provide secretarial support duties including the provision of an efficient audio and copy-typing service within the practice. This includes the appropriate lay out and accurate typing of letters, reports, patient referrals etc. Are competent users of Microsoft Office Become competent in the use of bespoke software packages including, e-RS and Accenda Gateway. Other software packages will be introduced from time to time. Training is available for all non-standard packages Sort and distribute mail both in and out, including the use of a mail franking system. This includes dealing with electronic mail coming in from hospitals Maintain adequate stocks of medical and general stationery Plan and book private medicals, ensuring that clinicians receive appropriate paperwork for review including the receipt of fees for such reports To work in accordance with written administration policies and procedures Undertake accurate filing of records, fax and photocopy as requested. Attend regular Patient Support team meetings To be part of the rota for extended hours cover of the administration function Ensure familiarisation with, and work in accordance with written policies and procedures so as to ensure ongoing successful registration with the Care Quality Commission Provide cover for other administration staff for holiday and sickness for which overtime will be paid Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Any other duties which may from time to time be requested by your line manager.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: We are seeking a compassionate and proactive Medical Receptionist to join our busy GP practice team. This is a key front-line role, supporting patients to access the right care, at the right time, from the right service. You will help patients navigate primary care services, community resources and external agencies, ensuring they receive appropriate, timely and coordinated support. Working closely with GPs, nurses, and the wider multidisciplinary team, you will act as a central point of contact for patients, helping to manage enquiries, signpost effectively, and improve overall patient experience. The role requires excellent communication skills, sound judgement, strong organisational ability, and a calm, professional approach in a fast-paced environment. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who is passionate about patient-centred care and wants to make a genuine difference within their local community. Act as the first point of contact for patient enquiries, gathering relevant information sensitively and accurately. Signpost patients to appropriate clinicians, services or community support in line with practice protocols. Support care coordination for patients with long-term conditions and complex needs. Process and manage appointment requests in line with triage guidance. Liaise with the wider multidisciplinary team to ensure seamless patient journeys. Maintain accurate clinical records and update patient information on the clinical system. Contribute to improving access, patient flow and overall patient experience. You will act as a first point of contact for patients and external agencies, responding to enquiries professionally and sensitively, whether in person, by telephone or electronically. You will gather relevant information, care navigate in line with practice protocols, and ensure patients are directed to the most appropriate clinician or service. You will also support home visit requests and liaise with community and secondary care providers where required. You will manage appointment systems effectively, including booking, amending and cancelling appointments, processing recalls and supporting demand management processes. This includes recording accurate information on the clinical system, supporting long-term condition monitoring and ensuring patients receive timely follow-up. The role also includes general administrative duties such as processing incoming and outgoing correspondence, scanning and coding documents, maintaining accurate patient records, and providing clerical support to the wider team. You will contribute to maintaining smooth day-to-day operations within the practice and undertake mandatory training as required.
